faq.q: What DPI should I use for photo prints?
faq.a: 300 DPI is the industry standard for high-quality photo prints. Most photo labs require 300 DPI. For large-format prints (posters, banners) viewed from >3m away, 150 DPI is acceptable.

faq.q: What is the difference between A4 and Letter?
faq.a: A4 (210×297mm) is the international standard used in most countries. Letter (8.5×11 inches / 216×279mm) is the US standard. Always check which your print service expects.

faq.q: My image is too small for 300 DPI — what should I do?
faq.a: If your source image has fewer pixels than the target DPI size, use our Image Upscaler tool first to enlarge it 2× or 4×, then come back to set the correct DPI.

faq.q: Should I download as PNG or JPG?
faq.a: For photos, JPG at quality 92+ is fine and produces smaller files. For text, line art, screenshots, or images with sharp edges, use PNG to avoid compression artifacts.

faq.q: Does this actually embed the DPI in the file?
faq.a: Yes. The Canvas API produces images with the correct pixel dimensions for the chosen DPI and paper size. When you open the file in Photoshop or your print lab's upload system, the dimensions will match the physical print size at the specified DPI.

faq.q: Can I use this for commercial printing?
faq.a: Yes. The output images are print-ready. For commercial printing, we recommend 300 DPI and JPG format (the industry standard). Always request a proof before a large print run.

faq.q: Is my image uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. All processing happens entirely in your browser. Your images never leave your device.
